items.desc: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.

items.title: Pope Leo urges men to respect wives amid Latin American femicide crisis
items.desc: Pope Leo XIV urged men to respect their wives as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America. The region recorded nearly 20,000 instances of women being killed over the past five years alone, most of them murdered by a current or former partner.

items.title: ‘10 times more painful’: Menstrual disorders fuel calls to ban tear gas at French protests
items.desc: French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests that have roiled France in recent weeks, sometimes causing grievous injuries. Thousands of accounts of women experiencing acutely painful periods and increased bleeding are further challenging assumptions that the chemical irritant carries only minor consequences.

items.title: 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games: Golden Double for Senegal
items.desc: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.

items.title: Diwali: Over one billion people mark victory of light over darkness
items.desc: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the deity celebrated during the festival, festivities included performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.

items.title: Paraguay: Senate impeached Peña rather than accept his offer to resign
items.desc: Paraguay's ousted president, Santiago Peña, has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Initially placed under house arrest, he has since been transferred to a military facility for his own safety. Nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts after regulators seized control of the online bank. Repayments are now under way, but protests continue as customers demand access to their money. Peña denies any wrongdoing. Jack Pownall reports.

items.title: Middle East live: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government
items.desc: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 28 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments from the Middle East.

items.title: Donald Trump wants UFC fighters as assistants
items.desc: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.

items.title: Israel's Arab-led parties gain influence
items.desc: Arab-led parties have endorsed Gadi Eisenkot despite his ruling out a coalition with them. Their support is driven by a shared goal: removing Benjamin Netanyahu from power. But could these parties ultimately hold the balance of power in forming Israel's next government? Antonia Kerrigan reports.

items.title: Gaza: Heavy rain inundates thousands of tents
items.desc: Heavy rainfall has flooded thousands of tents sheltering displaced Palestinians across the Gaza Strip, including in Deir al-Balah. Residents say overflowing sewage has mixed with the floodwater, further worsening already dire living conditions. Families are struggling to salvage their belongings, building makeshift earthen barriers and trying to drain the water by hand. Many have seen essential items soaked and rendered unusable, adding to the hardship faced by those already displaced.

items.title: Poland launches terrorism probe into mass shooting in Krakow
items.desc: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis claim attack on Aramco skyscraper in Riyadh
items.desc: A skyscraper belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco was hit by a Houthi-claimed attack on Sunday, blowing out windows across several floors but causing no casualties. The Iran-aligned group has repeatedly targeted Aramco facilities and infrastructure.

items.title: Tenerife honour teammate Jesus De Miguel with tearful tribute
items.desc: Tenerife’s stadium filled up with thousands of mourners on Saturday where they held a tearful tribute to striker Jesus De Miguel, who passed away after colliding with a goalkeeper during a match, subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest. "To speak of you in the past tense ​is tremendously unfair," team captain Enric Gallego said.

items.title: New Zealand's knife-edge parliamentary election delivers no clear winner
items.desc: No clear winner was produced in New Zealand’s legislative elections Saturday, setting up the two main blocs – Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition and opposition leader Chris Hipkins' left-wing alliance – for weeks of political wrangling to attempt to cobble together a majority. Hipkins said that while New Zealanders had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said".

items.title: Gunman kills six in Krakow, three more bodies found at his house
items.desc: A chilling new discovery in Poland, where three bodies have reportedly been found inside the Krakow gunman's home. That's in addition to six people killed and sixteen wounded when the attacker opened fire in the city's historic square. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has now declared the shooting an act of terrorism, saying Poland has never experienced anything quite like it. The 25-year-old suspect, described by authorities as holding radical far-right views, was shot by police.

items.title: France beat Fiji to reclaim top spot in Nations Championship
items.desc: France trashed Fiji 54-17 on Saturday to return to the top of the northern hemisphere Nations Championship standings.

items.title: 粮农组织：10月食品价格指数回落
items.desc: 联合国粮食及农业组织周五发布数据显示，10月食品价格指数环比下降1.2%。进口需求减弱推动谷物、乳制品和肉类价格下跌，抵消了食糖和植物油价格上涨的影响。

items.title: 人权遭受全面限制，阿富汗面临日益加剧的人道主义危机
items.desc: 一名联合国高级官员周五表示，塔利班重掌政权五年多以来，阿富汗正处于一个“艰难的十字路口”。相对的稳定与安全正受到脆弱的经济、对人权的全面限制以及严峻的人道主义需求的影响。

items.title: 针对记者的滥用诉讼增多，法律保护亟待加强

items.title: 来自北极冰海深处的呼声：世界应当相信科学
items.desc: 在漫长的极夜中，一支科考队正随海冰缓缓漂流，记录北极正在发生的深刻变化。海冰逐渐消融，油轮驶入北极航道。这片遥远的冰海正经历着海冰消融与航运活动增加的双重变化，而其影响远不止于北极。在一场跨越千里的视频对话中，北极科考队与联合国秘书长共同探讨了这些变化背后的全球气候挑战，以及为什么在气候危机日益严峻的今天，相信科学尤为重要。

items.title: 难民署：近9000万被迫流离失所者面临严重气候风险
items.desc: 联合国难民署周五发布报告指出，全球近9000万被迫流离失所者生活在气候灾害风险严重的国家，占全球被迫流离失所人口的约四分之三。

items.title: 国际原子能机构考察团审查俄罗斯核与辐射安全监管框架
items.desc: 国际原子能机构专家组周五表示，俄罗斯拥有能力强、独立的核与辐射安全监管机构，监管体系成熟，并重视安全文化。但监管部门之间的协调、人员规划和培训等方面仍有改进空间。

items.title: 古特雷斯：多边主义面临五项考验 国际社会必须让武力服从法律
items.desc: 联合国秘书长古特雷斯周五在西班牙萨拉曼卡大学发表演讲时指出，当今多边主义正面临和平、尊严、公平、气候正义以及技术管控五项决定性考验。他强调，国际社会必须坚持共同规则，让武力服从法律，让权力服务于公共利益。
